summary: Eisaku Okada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014). He held posts at JSPS (attested 2014), Koyasan University (attested 2014, 2026), and Kyoto University (attested 2015).
Eisei Kojima is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1976, he is attested as a professor at Ryukoku University and president of Doho University.

Eishu Miyazaki (1913–1997) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Rissho University (~1933–1938) under Gyoo Kageyama, later holding posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (~1949–1983).
Eishun Fushimi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.
Eivind Kahrs works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge (attested 2010) and served on the council of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen Kyōdan.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Gyosei Shoin, Doshisha, Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College, under Hiroshi Tsuchiya, Enryo Inoue, Unsho Shaku, Kozen Shaku, Hozan Saeki, and Sarat Chandra Das. He held posts at Toyo University and Toyo Bunko.
Ekyo Uno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Uno held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and Honganji-ha Shōgakuin (attested 1998).
Elaine Fisher is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies at Columbia University (attested 2010) and joined the faculty at Stanford University (attested 2026).

Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. After studying at Girton College (~1970–1973) and the University of Oxford (~1973–1974), she served at the University of Warwick (~1989–2012) as emerita professor in Education Studies.

Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Roger Brown, and held posts at Connecticut College, Brown University (~1970–1971), and the University of California, Berkeley (from 1971).
Elena Bashir specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1979–1988) and became Senior Lecturer Emerita at the University of Chicago (2000).

Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian history at Sapienza University of Rome (~1967–1971) under Luciano Petech. She became an associate professor at Sapienza University of Rome in 1980.
Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

Elena Mucciarelli is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen. She held positions at the University of Tübingen (2016–2017) and the University of Groningen (from 2020).

Eli Franco (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Tel Aviv, EHESS, EPHE, Paris Nanterre, and Hamburg under Charles Malamoud, and held chairs and posts at Kyoto, La Trobe, Vienna, and Leipzig (2004–2021).

Elijah Ary (born 1972) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and Geshe Karma Sonam.

Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago, Harvard, and Columbia, and held faculty posts at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006).

Elisa Freschi (born 1977) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raffaele Torella. She has held posts at Sapienza University of Rome, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the University of Vienna, and the University of Toronto (from ~2021).
Elisa Ganser is an Indology scholar attested in 2026 as a Lektorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and a visiting researcher at the University of Zurich.
